([[Minneapolis|Minneapolis, Minnesota]]) | college = [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford]] (2019–2020) | highlights = * [[Pac-12 Conference|Pac-12]] All-Freshman Team (2020) }} '''Tyrell Terry''' (born September 28, 2000) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford Cardinal]]. ==High school career== Terry played basketball for [[DeLaSalle High School (Minneapolis)|DeLaSalle High School]] in [[Minneapolis|Minneapolis, Minnesota]]. As a freshman, he helped his team win the Class 3A state championship and become the first team in Minnesota history to capture five straight titles.{{cite web |last1=La Vaque |first1=David |title=First with five straight: DeLaSalle makes state history winning 3A championship |url=https://www.mnbasketballhub.com/news_article/show/624470-first-with-five-straight-delasalle-makes-state-history-winning-3a-championship |website=MN Basketball Hub |accessdate=February 21, 2020 |date=March 12, 2016}} Terry also led DeLaSalle to 3A state titles as a sophomore and senior.{{cite web |last1=La Vaque |first1=David |title=DeLaSalle crushes Princeton in Class 3A boys' basketball semifinals |url=http://www.startribune.com/delasalle-crushes-princeton-in-class-3a-boys-basketball-semifinals/507502302/ |website=[[Star Tribune]] |accessdate=February 21, 2020 |date=March 21, 2019}} As a junior, [[Columbia Heights High School]] ended DeLaSalle's streak of state titles in the semifinals. In his senior season, he was named a finalist for the [[Minnesota Mr. Basketball]] award.{{cite web |last1=Max |first1=Mike |title=Tyrell Terry & Jamison Battle, DeLaSalle’s Dynamic Duo, Aim For 1 Last State Title |url=https://minnesota.cbslocal.com/2019/02/15/tyrell-terry-jamison-battle-delasalles-dynamic-duo-aim-for-1-last-state-title/ |website=[[WCCO-TV]] |accessdate=February 21, 2020 |date=February 15, 2019}} He scored 22 points in the 2019 title game. ==College career== On November 6, 2019, Terry made his debut for Stanford, recording 14 points, four rebounds and four assists in a 73–62 win over [[Montana Grizzlies basketball|Montana]].{{cite web |last1=Eymer |first1=Rick |title=Stanford men battle past Montana in basketball opener |url=https://www.mercurynews.com/2019/11/06/stanford-men-battle-past-montana-in-basketball-opener/ |website=[[The Mercury News]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |accessdate=March 26, 2020 |date=November 6, 2019}} On November 21, he registered his first career [[double (basketball)|double-double]] with 21 points and 10 rebounds in an 81–50 victory over [[William & Mary Tribe men's basketball|William & Mary]].{{cite web |last1=Eymer |first1=Rick |title=It was Terry's night to shine for Stanford men's basketball |url=https://www.paloaltoonline.com/news/2019/11/21/it-was-terrys-night-to-shine-for-stanford-mens-basketball |website=[[Palo Alto Weekly]] |accessdate=March 26, 2020 |date=November 21, 2019}} In his next game, Terry had another double-double, posting 20 points and 11 rebounds in a 73–54 win over [[Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball|Oklahoma]].{{cite web |last1=Stewart |first1=Savanna |title=Tyrell Terry, men’s hoops shine in rout of Oklahoma |url=https://www.stanforddaily.com/2019/11/26/tyrell-terry-mens-hoops-shine-in-rout-of-oklahoma/ |website=[[The Stanford Daily]] |accessdate=March 26, 2020 |date=November 26, 2019}} On January 13, 2020, he was named [[Pac-12 Conference]] Freshman of the Week after averaging 16.5 points, 7.5 rebounds and 4.5 assists per game in wins over [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington]] and [[Washington State Cougars men's basketball|Washington State]].{{cite web |title=California's Bradley, Stanford's Terry voted Pac-12 Men's Basketball Players of the Week |url=https://pac-12.com/article/2020/01/13/californias-bradley-stanfords-terry-voted-pac-12-mens-basketball-players-week |publisher=[[Pac-12 Conference]] |accessdate=March 26, 2020 |date=January 13, 2020}} On February 26, Terry scored a career-high 27 points with seven three-pointers to lead his team past [[Utah Utes men's basketball|Utah]], 70–62.{{cite web |title=Tyrell Terry pours in 27 points to lead Stanford past Utah |url=https://www.sfchronicle.com/collegesports/article/Tyrell-Terry-pours-in-27-points-to-lead-Stanford-15088054.php |website=[[San Francisco Chronicle]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |accessdate=March 26, 2020 |date=February 26, 2020}} This performance, along with a 12-point effort to upset 21st-ranked [[Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball|Colorado]], helped him earn Pac-12 Freshman of the Week honors on March 2.{{cite web |title=Stanford's Tyrell Terry takes home penultimate Pac-12 Men's Basketball Freshman of the Week award |url=https://pac-12.com/videos/stanfords-tyrell-terry-takes-home-penultimate-pac-12-mens-basketball-freshman-week-award |publisher=[[Pac-12 Conference]] |accessdate=March 26, 2020 |date=March 2, 2020}} At the end of the regular season, Terry was named to the Pac-12 All-Freshman Team and All-Pac-12 honorable mention.{{cite web |last1=Avalon |first1=Grant |title=Terry, Wills, da Silva earn Pac-12 Honors |url=https://www.ruleoftree.com/2020/3/9/21172439/terry-wills-da-silva-earn-pac-12-honors |publisher=Rule of Tree |accessdate=March 26, 2020 |date=March 9, 2020}} As a freshman, he averaged 14.7 points, 4.5 rebounds, 3.2 assists and 1.4 steals per game. His shooting accuracy, with a 40.8 three-point percentage and team-high 89.1 free throw percentage, helped him gain attention as a [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) prospect.{{cite web |last1=Pfeifer |first1=Ben |title=Tyrell Terry’s skill makes him worthy of a lottery selection |url=https://fansided.com/2020/02/20/2020-nba-draft-tyrell-terry-skill-makes-him-worthy-lottery-selection/ |publisher=FanSided |accessdate=March 26, 2020 |date=February 20, 2020}} Following the season, Terry declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]].{{cite news |last1=Wojnarowski |first1=Adrian |title=Sources: Stanford's Tyrell Terry plans to enter NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/29001259/sources-stanford-tyrell-terry-plans-enter-nba-draft |accessdate=April 7, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=April 6, 2020}} On July 31, Terry announced he was remaining in the draft.{{cite news |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |title=Stanford freshman Tyrell Terry to stay in 2020 NBA draft pool |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/29572285/stanford-freshman-tyrell-terry-stay-2020-nba-draft-pool |accessdate=July 31, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=July 31, 2020}} ==Professional career== It was reported that Terry “broke a record” for a basketball IQ test administered by several NBA front offices in the 2020 offseason.{{cite web | url=https://twitter.com/BryanKalbrosky/status/1272909355587944448}} ==National team career== In 2018, Terry played for the [[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|United States]] at the [[Albert Schweitzer Tournament]], a U18 tournament in [[Mannheim]], Germany. In five games, he averaged 6.6 points, 2.6 assists and 1.8 steals per game and helped his team finish in seventh place in the tournament.{{cite web |title=Cardinal Inks Terry |url=https://gostanford.com/news/2018/11/14/mens-basketball-cardinal-inks-terry.aspx |publisher=Stanford Athletics |accessdate=March 26, 2020 |date=November 14, 2018}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===College=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2019–20 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2019–20]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2019–20 Stanford Cardinal men's basketball team|Stanford]] | 31 || 31 || 32.6 || .441 || .408 || .891 || 4.5 || 3.2 || 1.4 || .1 || 14.6 {{S-end}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[https://gostanford.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/tyrell-terry/16485 Stanford Cardinal bio] {{DEFAULTSORT:Terry, Tyrell}} [[Category:2000 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Minnesota]] [[Category:Point guards]] [[Category:Sportspeople from Minneapolis]] [[Category:Stanford Cardinal men's basketball players]]
